claims.text: The position of a transition-metal catalyst's d-band center relative to the Fermi level governs its catalytic activity and selectivity.
A d-band center closer to the Fermi level makes reactant binding and activation more favorable.
More favorable reactant binding and activation caused by a closer d-band center enhance catalytic activity and selectivity.
Alloying a transition metal with a secondary metal can systematically tune its d-band-center position.
The d-band center can be tuned by alloying without major changes in catalyst morphology.
The alloying-induced d-band-center shift changes the electronic properties of the catalyst surface.
Moving the d-band center closer to the Fermi level enhances overlap between metal d states and reactant orbitals.
Enhanced overlap with reactant orbitals lowers activation energies for bond formation or cleavage.
Lower activation energies increase catalytic activity and may improve selectivity for desired products.
Alloy catalysts whose d-band centers are closer to the Fermi level will have higher turnover frequencies than the pure-metal baseline.
Such alloy catalysts will exhibit altered selectivity favoring desired products relative to the pure-metal baseline.
The proposed relationship is expected to apply to extended metal surfaces and well-defined nanoparticles for which the d-band model is applicable.
The relationship may fail when particle-size effects, support effects, or quantum confinement dominate.
Geometric strain, surface reconstruction, and adsorbate-adsorbate interactions may affect the relationship between d-band-center position and catalytic performance.
UPS or XPS can be used to determine the d-band-center positions in the proposed catalyst series.
A lack of systematic correlation between d-band-center position and activity or selectivity would falsify the hypothesis.
